--- title: "Sustained attention" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · F_EJEC_ATENCIÓN_ATENCION_SOSTENIDA" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (E · Decision with response time; quality class B). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea F_EJEC_ATENCIÓN_ATENCION_SOSTENIDA`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Atención sostenida*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/F_EJEC_ATENCIÓN_ATENCION_SOSTENIDA.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class B.** It has enough data to be described, but it lacks some of the guarantees of class A (stability across time points, item-level reliability or validity). Use with caution and not for individual decisions. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Sustained attention, from age 4 to 8 (3,406 administrations in 4 cohorts). Stability across time points ρ = .04. AUC .43–.56 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1865 | | Battery | UNED | | Format | rapid naming of a series | | Items | 50 | | Task family | E · Decision with response time | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | This task allows obtaining an index of executive-attentional inhibitory ability from a simple task of decision about word-image correspondence. An image is shown on the centre of the screen followed by a name sound. Participants are required to respond by clicking the left mouse button if name and image correspond or the right mouse button if there is not correspondence. | ![Example of the screen format (2018 screenshot; not necessarily an item from this task).](../../figuras/pantallas/formato_ran.png){width=45%} ## Theoretical framework **Visual-attentional span** is the number of visual elements processed simultaneously within a string. On the platform, a string of letters, numbers or symbols is briefly presented and the child chooses what they saw. **Serial search** asks whether there is an O among groups of Qs of different sizes. The **sustained attention** task (UNED battery) consists of 50 trials in which the child decides whether the name they hear matches the picture; despite its name, the catalog describes it as an index of inhibitory control. Reading requires processing several letters at once and maintaining attention along the line. **What the evidence says:** - **Visual-attentional span predicts reading beyond phonemic awareness.** In 417 French children in Grades 1, 3 and 5, it predicted reading independently of phonemic awareness, especially for irregular words [@bosse2009span]. Orthographic depth modulates how this attention is distributed: advanced bilinguals reading in French and Basque distributed it more evenly than those reading in Spanish and Basque [@antzaka2018depth]. - **Visual search is associated with reading, with small samples.** In 16 children with dyslexia and 16 controls, slow serial search was associated with visual-attentional span and with irregular word reading, not with phonology [@lallier2013search]. Visual scanning measured in preschool predicted learning to read in Italian children [@ferretti2008scanning]. - **Sustained attention is related more to comprehension than to word reading.** In 245 poor readers in Grades 4 and 5, it explained unique variance in comprehension, but not in reading accuracy or fluency [@macdonald2021sustained]. The evidence is weaker than for phonological processes and there are almost no studies in Spanish. **What our data show.** - **Letter and symbol subtests.** With 6–10 points and a single session, AUC from .47 to .61: separately they are not interpretable. - **Numbers and letters (36 items, ages 4–5).** α = .60 and AUC of .66–.67 against persistent difficulty and of .65 against later low comprehension. It is the best in the family, as expected of alphanumeric stimuli. - **Numbers (16 items).** α = .56 and almost zero stability across school years (ρ = .05–.19). AUC from .54 to .69. - **Serial search.** α = .74, ceiling of 11–20% and AUC from .58 to .63. - **Sustained attention.** Despite an α of .95, it shows no validity: extreme ceiling (median 45 out of 50), stability of ρ = .03–.16, null correlation with the other domains and AUC from .43 to .56. It should not be used until the data have been reviewed. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.2| 2013| 186|2017/18 | 567| 559| 8| 23| | 4.3| 2011| 141|2015/16 | 7| 0| 7| 1| | 5.2| 2012| 187|2017/18 | 326| 323| 0| 16| | 5.3| 2010| 140|2015/16 | 866| 254| 610| 36| | 6.2| 2011| 188|2017/18 | 766| 0| 766| 30| | 7.3| 2010| 190|2017/18 | 402| 151| 251| 29| | 8.3| 2010| 640|2018/19 | 472| 100| 371| 23| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 4.2| 559| 2013| 44.58| 4.52| 45| -3.89| 0| 6.62| | 5.2| 323| 2012| 42.41| 9.49| 45| -3.39| 0| 1.86| | 5.3| 254| 2010| 44.23| 1.80| 44| -0.82| 0| 0.39| | 7.3| 151| 2010| 44.13| 4.25| 45| -7.00| 0| 0.00| | 8.3| 100| 2010| 43.48| 7.94| 45| -4.51| 0| 2.00| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Warning | |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------------| | 4.2| 559|25–50 |6–50 |extreme value: check | | 5.2| 323|4–50 |2–50 | | | 5.3| 254|39.5–48 |34–50 |extreme value: check | | 7.3| 151|27–48 |3–48 |extreme value: check | | 8.3| 100|5–50 |5–50 | | ## Reliability Stability across time points in the same children: ρ from .03–.16 (median .04, 3 pairs of time points). Internal consistency in the 2021 analyses: α = .95. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|-----:|----:| | 2010| 5.3| 7.3| 329| 0.03| 0.16| | 2010| 5.3| 8.3| 351| -0.01| 0.03| | 2010| 7.3| 8.3| 220| -0.03| 0.04| ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Letter knowledge (4.2, r = .14); Word and text reading (5.2, r = .01); Letter knowledge (5.3, r = .06); Word and text reading (6.2, r = -.00); Reading comprehension (7.3, r = .05); Word and text reading (8.3, r = -.05). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .43–.56. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .47–.57. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_F_EJEC_ATENCIÓN_ATENCION_SOSTENIDA_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .44–.57 (5 time points; 118–255 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|----:|----:|---:|----:|---:|---:|---:| | 4.2| 559| 2013| 38.0| 43.0| 44| 44.0| 45| 46| 48| | 5.2| 323| 2012| 10.3| 39.4| 43| 44.0| 45| 46| 47| | 5.3| 254| 2010| 41.0| 42.0| 43| 44.0| 44| 45| 46| | 6.2| 766| 2011| 42.0| 43.0| 44| 44.0| 45| 46| 47| | 7.3| 151| 2010| 41.5| 43.0| 43| 44.0| 45| 45| 46| | 8.3| 100| 2010| 42.9| 44.0| 44| 44.8| 45| 45| 46| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_F_EJEC_ATENCIÓN_ATENCION_SOSTENIDA_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.2| 567| -0.080| 0.056| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.2| 564| 0.049| 0.559| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.2| 567| -0.004| 0.921| |School (ICC) | 4.2| 567| 0.071| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.2| 300| 0.001| 0.986| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.2| 324| -0.121| 0.284| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.2| 320| -0.036| 0.521| |School (ICC) | 5.2| 326| 0.445| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.3| 866| -0.047| 0.166| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.3| 826| -0.027| 0.700| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.3| 825| 0.024| 0.493| |School (ICC) | 5.3| 866| 0.145| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.2| 728| 0.019| 0.603| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.2| 765| 0.081| 0.256| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.2| 763| -0.057| 0.113| |School (ICC) | 6.2| 766| 0.020| | |School SES (ρ) | 7.3| 402| -0.065| 0.196| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 7.3| 399| -0.030| 0.761| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 7.3| 399| 0.081| 0.105| |School (ICC) | 7.3| 402| 0.057| | |School SES (ρ) | 8.3| 472| -0.058| 0.207| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 8.3| 465| 0.042| 0.645| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 8.3| 464| -0.035| 0.454| |School (ICC) | 8.3| 472| 0.364| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Sustained attention” (code 1865; UNED battery) assesses sustained attention. The child names a series of familiar stimuli on the screen as quickly as possible, and the examiner records correct responses and errors. It comprises 50 items. The time limit is 180 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012 and 2013 cohorts it was administered in 7 sessions, from 4 to 8 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .95 (N = 2,960, 50 items). Stability across time points was ρ = .03–.16. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .47–.57. ## Pending issues - Extreme value at 4.2, 5.3, 7.3: the maximum or minimum is more than 2 SD away from P99 or P1. Check in the raw data (possible timing or recording error). - Estabilidad muy baja entre aplicaciones (ρ = .04): revisar los datos (códigos, versiones o tiempos) antes de usar la tarea *(Spanish)* - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
